# Power — Changelog Archive

_Older releases, moved out of the add-on `CHANGELOG.md` so Home Assistant's Changelog dialog stays fast: it renders the whole file. `scripts/roll-changelog.mjs` keeps the newest releases that fit in 32 KiB in `CHANGELOG.md` and moves each older one here unedited, newest first; CI fails once `CHANGELOG.md` passes 48 KiB. (v1.38.3 first trimmed the file to its 20 newest releases; with only a sentence to hold it there, it grew back to 109 releases and 330 KB by v1.187.21.)_

_Restored 2026-09-06: the v1.131.2 release commit truncated `CHANGELOG.md` to a single entry (`open(p,'w')` truncates before the `open(p).read()` in the same expression runs), destroying 145 entries — v1.22.0 through v1.131.1. Recovered from git history and re-archived here. Nothing was lost; it was recoverable because every prior revision is in the commit history._

## 1.196.0

### The overnight write charges to the line the plan is sized on; the no-plan and force-charge warnings say why; the cost ceiling counts the measured sun

**Night charge**

- With the islanded-outage cushion (or the cushion disabled), the overnight reserve write is now solved on the test the plan is sized on: the pack at the window close against the reserve floor plus the outage cushion. It was solved on a whole-house walk to the next charge window. On this plant that walk falls below the line from any starting level, so every charge night asked for about 73-100% and wrote the 50% maximum. A resilience night now writes the cushion line, rounded up to the next whole percent. For example, a 16% floor with a 4 h, 2.62 kW, x1.25 cushion now writes 32% where it wrote 50%, and the expected draw falls from about 27.9 kWh to about 10 kWh. `ARB_OUTAGE_CUSHION_HOURS` is unchanged.
- A cost night writes its cost target where that is higher than the line, so a ceiling under 50% is written as itself (40% for a 40.3% ceiling, where it wrote 50%). A night limited by the charge rate writes the target, never the lower arrival the window can reach. The legacy band, the outage backup leg and the mid-day leg's reserve are unchanged.
- Of the 1,104 recorded plan cases, 431 setpoints move, all on the islanded-outage cushion. 157 resilience charge nights write a lower reserve (median 13 points), 17 cost charge nights write lower (median 7 points), and 5 cost nights limited by the charge rate write higher (their cost target). No charge night writes under its line, or under 50% where its line is higher. No buy and no requirement changes.
- The cushion is counted on the panel's nameplate pool, and the reserve percent is a share of the packs' measured capacity (about 0.944 of nameplate). The written line therefore holds about that share of the counted cushion above the reserve (options guide; reference chapter 15 part 1).
- The reserve sentence says the panel accepts a backup reserve only up to 50% only when the ask is above 50%. Before, it was also printed for asks such as 40.3% or 44.2% that were written as 40% or 44%.
- The force-charge failure warning, and its log line, now name the Core in each slot that did not take Charge Now. They say when that Core is offline in the cloud, and name its work mode or its own backup reserve when that differs from the other Cores driven that night. For example: "slot(s) 3 (Core 5 — work mode 3 (time-of-use), where the other Cores read 0 (default); its own backup reserve 60%, where the other Cores read 50%)". The warning then suggests comparing those settings in the EcoFlow app. Labels never contain serial digits. The slot-to-Core mapping comes from the fresh panel reading; the settings are each Core's last report. The morning summary keeps slot numbers.
- The "Night-charge: no plan tonight" push names what refused the plan. For example: "the forecast/telemetry basis is incomplete: PV band coverage 72% < 78% (…)", or "SoC telemetry incoherent (% vs remaining/full mismatch)". A night with no panel reading says the panel's pool readings are unavailable. The reason is on the plan as `basisBlockedBy`, which was declared but never set; it is now set on every refused plan and absent on a complete one. The mid-day preview's "not armed" line and its "no plan" push carry it too.

**Write-readiness gate**

- The realized half of the engine-fault strike is now graded on what the plan claims. With the islanded-outage cushion (or the cushion disabled), the plan claims only that the pool at the window close holds the reserve floor plus the cushion it sized (`cushion_line_soc_pct`). The verdict was the lowest pool over the 16 hours after the close against the reserve floor plus `ARB_OUTAGE_CUSHION_PCT`, measured after the reserve has reverted to the floor. With the write at the line, that verdict would have counted almost every actuated resilience night as a strike and held the gate at `BLOCKED`. On the 2026-10-12 fixture the 32% write has a P50 morning low of about 23.6%, against 16 + 15 = 31%; with a 2.0 kW island the 28% write is under 31% at the close itself.
- On such a night `cushion_breached` is now the pool measured at the window close (new ledger column `window_close_soc_pct`, the median reading over the window's last 15 minutes) under the line, with 0.05 points allowed for rounding. Without that reading the night is clean when the lowest pool after the close holds the line; otherwise the verdict is unknown. The gate derives the verdict again from the row's columns and keeps the stored flag where the columns cannot decide (fail-closed). It counts the stored flags it overrules in `realizedStrikesSetAside`. A night whose line is above the panel's 50% reserve maximum, with no force-charge to carry the pool past it, now reads as breached: the plan claims a cushion the write cannot reach, because `cushionShortfall` does not count the write envelope (4 of the year fixture's 199 islanded evening charges with no disclosed shortfall; the old rule passed them). The legacy band, the mid-day two-leg row and rows without a recorded line keep the earlier verdict. `score_notes` states the reading against the line. `CURRENT_ALGO_VERSION` is unchanged, so no night leaves the readiness count.

**Night charge (cost mode)**

- The cost ceiling's morning-solar headroom now de-biases the median PV as well as the house load. It uses the median realized/forecast PV ratio from the night ledger (1 + `pv_err_frac`), over forecast-tier nights whose PV verdict stands, whose forecast was at least 5 kWh, and whose pool did not reach the charge taper. On those days output is curtailed, so their actual PV measures nothing.
- Like the load factor, the PV factor only widens the headroom (at least x1, at most x1.3). It needs 5 nights and takes full effect at 10. It never raises an hour's median PV past that hour's P90. On the 2026-10-12 fixture, ten nights at x1.095 lower the ceiling and the force-charge stop from 56.6% to 50.4%, and the expected buy from about 11.6 to 5.1 kWh.
- New plan fields: `costSurplusPvFactor`, `costSurplusPvSamples`. New ledger columns: `cost_surplus_pv_factor`, `cost_surplus_pv_samples`, `actual_max_soc_pct` and `pv_saturated`. When only the PV term is de-biased, the load factor is recorded as 1 with its nights.

**Unchanged**

- The runway, SoC and floor alarms do not read the write setpoint. The reserve write still reverts at the window close. Cost mode with a ceiling of 50% or more still writes 50% plus force-charge. The analytics PV forecast that feeds the runway and the alarms is unchanged.
- Charge and hold plans carry no `basisBlockedBy` key (cost-mode plans gain only the two PV-factor fields above).

**Tests**

- New: `setpointOneTest.test.ts`, `forceChargeFailedCore.test.ts`, `noPlanReason.test.ts`, `costCeilingPvDebias.test.ts` and `realizedCushionAtClose.test.ts` (an M5 resilience night, written 32% with a ~23.6% morning low, through the gate: no strike; a pool under its line at the close still strikes, including a line above the 50% envelope). `middayAnnounce.test.ts` covers the mid-day "no plan" reason.
- `legacyIdentity.golden.json` is regenerated on purpose, with an `_amended` note: 870 of 1,104 digests move against 1.195.0, by the setpoints (431), the refused plans' `basisBlockedBy` (132) and the cost plans' PV-factor keys (563). The truncation sentence alone moves no case. `overnightTextGolden.json` is regenerated in its evening entries only, and one reserve-only "toward" case is added.
- The 1.194.0 test that holds the charge leg to its direction now compares against the planner without the charge leg but with this release's setpoint (new `legacyIdentity.withoutChargeLeg.figures.json`), because 1.192.0's setpoints on the islanded-outage cushion were a walk. Every assertion holds. 95 buys rise and one hold becomes a charge, as before. 108 expected buys rise and 64 setpoints move, 5 of them down; when 1.194.0 measured them against 1.192.0 the figures were 118, 264 and 16. A new test checks the release against 1.192.0: no buy and no requirement falls. 85 expected buys rise; the 122 that fall, and the 381 setpoints that fall, are all on the islanded-outage cushion.
- New harness `scripts/mutate-v1196-night.mjs` (68 mutants; 17 on the realized verdict). Anchors are re-pointed in `mutate-v1187-1f.mjs`, `mutate-ledger-legibility.mjs`, `mutate-zero-cushion.mjs` and `mutate-readiness-gate.mjs`.

### The forecast skill measures each past day on that day's Cores

**Forecast skill (PV band, night-charge basis gate)**

- On the forecast-skill path, a home Core with no readings on a day now makes that day a coverage gap, as it already did for the PV bias factor. The hindcast used to take a Core's first reading inside the 30-day window as the day it joined (v1.93.0/v1.94.0). A Core already dark when the window began, or Cores returning on different days after a fleet-wide outage, then had their missing share scored as a forecast miss: +50% a day with one of three Cores dark, +200% with two. On a 7-day fixture with one of three Cores dark for the first three days, MAE and bias now read 0 kWh and 1.00 (were 1.93 kWh and 0.86).
- Each past day is now measured on the Cores the pool membership record (`membership-history.json`) shows as wired that day, not on today's Cores applied to 30 days of history. The recorder now stores the panel's slot table with each entry.
  - A day before a like-for-like swap (a Core moved into the slot a departing Core held, taking over its PV array) is scored on that day's own Cores and marked `predecessorCores`.
  - A day on which the pool lacked a current Core's array is marked `offRoster` and left out of the error, the bias factor and the PV band calibration. This covers days before a Core was added through an empty slot, a swap recorded before slot tables existed, and the day of a change.
  - Membership flickers under 15 minutes are ignored.
  - Days before the record are scored on telemetry coverage alone and counted in `unrecordedRosterDays`.
- A pre-swap day is scored on the departed Core only if a fresh panel reading confirmed the record through that day. The recorder stamps the newest entry (`confirmedMs`) on a fresh reading of every panel, at most once an hour. A swap made while the panel was cloud-offline or the add-on was stopped is recorded only when the panel next reads fresh. The days in between are `offRoster`, not scored on the departed Core's bench rows.
- After a Core is added, the night-charge basis gate counts only days measured on the new set of Cores, so it stays closed until 14 such days are scored (at least two weeks). A like-for-like swap loses the day of the swap and any unconfirmed day before it. A removal loses none.

**Unchanged**

- The PV bias factor on the runway and alarm paths: its coverage call and its output are unchanged.
- `membership-history.json` keeps its format. The new `slots` and `confirmedMs` fields are optional. The newest existing entry gains its slot table on the first rollup after the update, and its stamp on the first fresh panel reading. Neither is a membership change for the curtailment freeze or the pack-DC round-trip check.

**Tests**

- `skillRoster.test.ts` (new) covers:
  - a dark Core and staggered returns, which are gaps;
  - swaps scored on that day's Cores, including a departed Core dark on a pre-swap day;
  - additions, which pause;
  - a swap hidden behind a stale panel, which is `offRoster`;
  - flicker folding, superset pools and days before the record;
  - the production reader and the confirmation stamp;
  - the recorder writing the slot table, and stamping only on a fresh panel reading.
- The tests in `pvCoverageGate.test.ts` and `darkCoreCoverage.test.ts` that asserted the join exemption now assert a gap.
- `mutate-skill-roster.mjs` (new): 29 mutants. `mutate-dark-core.mjs` drops mutants v and vi, whose guard is gone.

## 1.195.0

### The forecast cards show the restored solar while Cores are offline; a held panel's circuits are no longer the house load; cell-spread mutes below 85% are bounded

**Dashboard**

- While home Cores were offline in the EcoFlow cloud, the 24-hour forecast card and the Predictive Insights forecast showed 0 kWh of solar, a projected low of 0% and a "Tight" outlook. Those are the figures the runway alarm uses, and they count only the Cores reporting live.
- The cards now show the solar and the projected state of charge rebuilt from each offline Core's own recorded production. This is the figure Home Assistant's forecast solar sensor already shows. The rebuilt state of charge starts from the same pool, carries the same hourly load and steps through the same function as the alarm's projection, the charge leg included, so with every Core reporting the two are equal hour by hour.
- A badge labels them: "Solar restored from N offline Cores' records". At a restart, while a Core listed online has not sent its first reading, it reads "Solar from N Cores' records (first reading pending)". Beside them:
  - the runway alarm's own figures: "Runway alarm basis (reporting Cores only): X kWh solar, low Y%"
  - its state-of-charge path, as a dashed line on the chart
  - an "Alarm-basis SoC" column in the hourly table
- Each hourly row's model / typical badge names the model that produced the figure shown.
- An offline Core with no recorded solar is not counted as restored. With no solar history at all, the solar tiles read "—" / "no PV history".
- `GET /api/forecast` gains `hoursDisplay`, `minProjectedSocDisplay`, `minProjectedSocTsDisplay` and `restoredCoreCount`.

**Runway**

- Before, when the panel's readings were held (a cloud replay or a stalled feed) and no load had been recorded for an hour, the runway took the panel's held circuit watts as the live house load, for as long as the hold lasted.
  - Circuits held at 9 kW projected the reserve floor in 2.8 h instead of 8.2 h: a false high-priority alarm.
  - Circuits held at 600 W hid a 6 kW draw: low instead of medium.
- Held readings are no longer used. The last recorded hour's load is carried for up to 2 h, as before. After that the runway reads unavailable until the panel reports again.
- While the house runway reads unavailable, the runway alarm keeps its state, as the other panels' runway alarms already did. Before, it re-armed: the hourly reminder stopped for the rest of the outage, and a short outage was followed by a fresh announcement.
- The load-shed advisor also keeps its last recommendation while the runway is unavailable. Before, it reported the runway healthy and cleared `load_shed_recommended` in the middle of a depletion.

**Cell spread (alarm path)**

- Below the 85% plateau, and with no SoC reading, a cell-spread critical silenced while the BMS balances now speaks 20 minutes after the spread first reached the line.
  - Before, the mute had no limit there. A 50-149 mV spread on a balancing pack stayed silent for as long as the BMS balanced. So did a spread alternating 55 / 45 / 45 mV, and a pack whose SoC read 84 / 85% on alternate readings.
  - Dips under the line do not restart the 20 minutes; only 20 minutes seen under 50 mV ends the session.
  - The session is carried across reading gaps of up to 60 minutes and across a restart. `vdiff-knee-state.json` gains `offFromMs`, `offQuietSinceMs` and `offKnee`, each written only while set.
- A 50-149 mV spread on a pack at 15% charge or less, within 10 points of its sibling packs, no longer sounds red at once.
  - On the steep bottom of the LFP curve, the cell with the least charge falls away and closes back on recharge. In the 2026-08-20 case, a healthy pack's red cleared in 6.7 minutes.
  - The critical stays on the card ("Low-charge cell spread."), is not pushed or sounded, and speaks after 20 minutes.
  - These get no low-charge grace:
    - a pack 10 or more points below its siblings (the alert names its charge and the sibling median)
    - a session that reached the line on any other reading
  - They page at once while the BMS is idle. While it reports balancing they are held by the balancing mute, and speak 20 minutes after the first crossing, like any balancing critical below 85%.
  - A spread of 150 mV or more pages at once, balancing or not.

**Unchanged**

- The runway alarm, the projected-dip and forecast-runtime alerts, the calendar's battery-dip event and Home Assistant's projected-low-SoC sensors still count only the Cores reporting live.
- Cell spread at 85% charge and above. The SoC ladder, the floor alarm and the stale alarms. "Reserve alarm blind" changes only across a restart (below).

**Tests**

- New: `forecastDisplayBasis.test.ts` covers the restored series and its SoC walk, isolation from every alarm input (by behaviour and by source), the restored model's flag, the restored-Core count, the cards' view and its wiring, the badge while a first reading is pending at a restart, and the charge leg on the restored walk (3,750 W restored against a 1,865.7 W drain stores 1,747.4 Wh an hour: 61.5% after the first hour, 94.9% after 24, against 97.7% at unity).
- New: `runwayHeldPanelLoad.test.ts` covers the live-load gate, the carry limit across a hold, and the runway alarm and load-shed advisor holding while the runway is unavailable.
- New: `cellSpreadOffPlateauSession.test.ts` covers the off-plateau session, the low-charge knee (a stranded pack while the BMS balances included), and both across a restart.
- The dark-fleet forecast golden gains the four display fields only; every earlier field is unchanged. `runwayChargeLegPins.test.ts` pins the charge leg inside the shared step and both walks' calls to it.
- New harnesses, all mutants killed:
  - `mutate-forecast-display-basis.mjs` (24)
  - `mutate-held-panel-load.mjs` (8)
  - `mutate-cell-spread-off-plateau.mjs` (19)
- Anchors re-pointed in older harnesses: `mutate-runway-card.mjs`, `mutate-v1187-1.mjs`, `mutate-v1187-2.mjs`, `mutate-v1187-19.mjs`, `mutate-v1187-a.mjs`, `mutate-v1191-1.mjs`, and `mutate-charge-leg.mjs` C-ii (the day walk's charge leg, now in the shared step).

### After a restart an owed all-clear is announced; a critical nobody heard is named when it returns; an announcement kept behind another alarm's retry is spoken

**After a restart**

- **An all-clear that was due when the add-on stopped is announced after the restart.** When an alarm the house had heard cleared, the add-on waits three minutes before announcing the all-clear (up to 16 minutes after a restart, and longer while a muted cell-imbalance critical holds it). A restart during that wait lost the all-clear. The add-on started with the alarm recorded as not heard and took the clear condition in silence, so the alarm stayed the last words. The wait is now saved with the condition record (`conditionHeldFrom` / `conditionHeldAt` in `broadcast-last.json`, and `conditionHeldFrom` in `/api/broadcast/status`). After a restart within an hour of the wait's start, the all-clear is announced once the condition has stayed clear for three minutes on a complete alert picture. If the picture is still incomplete when the post-restart decision closes, the clear condition is taken in silence, as for an alarm heard before a restart. These alarms all count as heard: one heard only as the tone (its speech failed), one heard only on the cordless, and one first heard during the wait itself (it cleared while its announcement was still playing, or its retry played during the wait). An alarm first heard during the wait no longer marks the record as heard while its clearing is held. A warning standing below it is therefore announced after a restart, not taken as its continuation. A condition that cleared while the add-on was stopped is still not announced.
- **"Reserve alarm blind" keeps its age for a panel dark more than a week.** A pool unreadable for more than 7 days lost its saved onset at a restart. The alarm disappeared for 15 minutes and came back as a warning for an hour, even when it had been critical. Only an onset claiming more than a year is now set aside, since it comes from a clock that was not set or an edited file. A panel that has not reported since the restart holds the post-restart decisions only until its own reserve-blind alarm is raised. The house panel has no reserve-blind alarm while it reports nothing, so it holds them until it reports.
- **A read-only data folder no longer carries an old "Reserve alarm blind" time.** On a read-only or failing disk, the saved time could be neither updated nor removed. A pool that read again after the last save was then carried after a restart as unreadable since before, and could raise a critical alarm with an inflated age. When the folder cannot be written at start-up, the saved times are not carried and never written back, and the log says so (`backup-pool: N pool-unknown onset(s) on file are not carried — …`). Each panel's reserve-blind clock then starts in the new process. The post-restart decisions wait by the same rule as above: for the house panel until it reports, and for any other panel until it reports or its own alarm is raised.

**Announcements**

- **A critical alarm nobody heard is announced when it comes back.** During one alarm, a critical that took another's place was treated as heard, even though only the first one was heard and the new one never reached the speakers. When it cleared and came back within three minutes, it was not announced again and was never named. A return is now announced when the alarm its words would name has not been heard during that alarm. A return refused by the two-minute gap is announced when the gap expires. Two alarms that return together, when the words name the one already heard, are still taken as a flicker. After a restart, an alarm found already announced counts as heard only the critical that announcement named. Another critical that stood beside it and returns alone is announced, as it would be without the restart.
- **An announcement that waited behind another alarm's retry is announced when that retry is done.** When the speakers could not play and a more serious announcement was already waiting to be retried, a less serious condition announcement was dropped. This lost a warning under a held critical, or a warning or an all-clear behind a battery-level or runway alarm. The same happened in the other order: a battery-level or runway alarm that failed while the condition announcement's own retry was waiting took that retry's place. The dropped announcement is now made once, when the other retry has played or given up, if the condition has not been committed at another level since. After a more serious condition alarm it waits the usual two minutes. Only one such announcement is kept at a time: the newest, unless the one already kept is more serious. A dedicated announcement kept the same way is not re-announced as a condition.

**Tests**

- `restartRecoveryAllClear.test.ts`:
  - A restart inside the dwell of a heard red, a heard yellow or a tone-only red announces the all-clear on a settled set. So does one after a red first made audible inside its own dwell: cleared while its announcement played (spoken or tone only), or with its retry played in the dwell.
  - A warning that stood below such a red is spoken after the restart, and the red flickering back restores its heard flag.
  - The critical back after the restart is the klaxon, with no all-clear before it.
  - A warning below the cleared red is spoken, whether it stands at the first tick or appears after it. At the first tick the owed hold is dropped at once, and the warning's clearing is an ordinary transition.
  - A warning re-committed under a resumed hold and never delivered is presented again when it returns inside the dwell.
  - On an unsettled set, the green is adopted silently when the decision closes.
  - Two restarts inside the hold still owe the all-clear, and the hold's age counts from its original start.
  - Nothing is owed after the green commits, or after the red flickers back, spoken or tone only (the cleared record is written to disk).
  - `restoredHeldDeescalation` checked by hand.
- `conditionRetryNewestWins.test.ts`:
  - A warning kept behind a red retry (held critical) is spoken after the gap. One behind a dedicated critical's retry is spoken with no gap.
  - An all-clear behind a dedicated warning's retry is spoken.
  - A warning, and an all-clear, whose own retry a dedicated alarm superseded are spoken.
  - A warning behind the dedicated alarm does not displace the more severe condition red kept before it. That red is named when its critical reads loud again.
  - A kept deferral is dropped when the condition has moved, and re-presented at once when the higher retry gives up.
  - A fired retry still queued plays first.
  - A dedicated notice is not re-presented.
  - `keptDeferralRepresent` checked by hand.
  - A critical that took a heard one's place undelivered is named when it returns, including after a gap refusal.
  - Still absorbed: a heard critical's flicker, two criticals returning together whose words name the heard one, and a red adopted by the red replay gate. A critical counted beside the adopted one and never named is spoken when it returns alone.
  - What was named audible resets with each red episode.
- `poolUnknownCarry.test.ts`:
  - A panel dark 7 days and an hour keeps its onset across a restart: critical "unreadable for 7 d" at once, carried at its first projection.
  - The pending rule ends when the dark panel's alarm is raised (inclusive at 15 min), and never for the pinned house panel. `darkPanelBlindRaised` tested.
  - A read-only directory carries nothing, keeps the panel pending, logs once, and writes nothing back once it is writable again. These tests skip only when a write probe of the directory succeeds, not on `poolUnknownDirWritable`'s answer.
  - `poolUnknownDirWritable`, the 366-day bound, and the alert monitor's wiring.
- New harness `scripts/mutate-restart-leftovers.mjs`: 42 mutants (F-i…F-xvi, N-i…N-viii, P-i…P-vii, D-i…D-v, O-i…O-vi).
- Re-pointed anchors: `mutate-v1187-4.mjs` H-i, H-ii, U-iii, U-iv, U-v, U-vii, U-viii, C-ix, C-xvi, C-xx, C-xxiii; `mutate-v1187-3h.mjs` B-i, B-ii; `mutate-v1187-b.mjs` xxiii, xxxv; `mutate-multi-panel.mjs` r11; `mutate-alert-monitor.mjs` xxiii; `mutate-broadcast.mjs` vii; `mutate-v1187-10-g3.mjs` C1-i.

## 1.194.0

### Solar surplus counts at the charge efficiency in the runway, the forecasts and the night-charge plan

**Runway and forecasts**

- The runway, the 24-hour and multi-day state-of-charge projections and the confidence band added solar energy beyond the house load to the battery pool in full. Charging the packs loses energy: on 29 measured sunny spans the pool gained 2–7% less than projected. A surplus now counts at the charge efficiency, the square root of `DISPATCH_ROUND_TRIP_EFFICIENCY` (0.927 by default), so a projection across a sunny day reads shorter. On a day with 44 kWh of surplus, the reserve crossing comes about 1 h sooner (22.8 h instead of 23.8 h) and the pool ends 3.2 kWh lower. An 18 kWh pool with two sunny hours ahead now reaches the reserve in 5.9 h instead of 6.1 h, which raises the medium runway alarm instead of the low one. The runway, forecast-runtime and forecast-soc-dip alerts can come up to about an hour earlier on a horizon that crosses a sunny day.
- The confidence band applies the charge efficiency to each path after its spread is added, and reads the trajectory's capacity with the same step.
- `DISPATCH_ROUND_TRIP_EFFICIENCY` (environment only, clamped 0.8–1) now also sets the alarm path's charge efficiency. Setting it to 1 puts the runway's and the projections' surplus credit back at unity; it also makes the night-charge and dispatch plans' charging lossless, so they buy less than before. No setting makes a projection longer than before.

**Night charge**

- The plan's walks count a surplus the same way: the worst-case sizing walk, the window walk, the expected-buy walks (expected carry, solar credit, force-charge timing) and the mid-day preview's held-import estimate. A trough that follows a sunny day's 31 kWh of surplus sits 2.25 kWh lower, and the buy that holds the line is 2.43 kWh larger.
- Of 1,104 recorded plan cases, 95 worst-case buys rise by up to 2.84 kWh (mean 0.44 kWh), 118 expected buys rise by up to 6.76 kWh (mean 1.17 kWh), and one hold becomes a 1.49 kWh charge. No buy, expected buy or requirement falls. 264 setpoints move, by −1.8 to +2.7 points. The 16 that fall are either charges limited by the window whose requirement rose, or holds whose projected arrival without a buy is now lower.
- The readiness gate keeps algorithm version 3, so nights already scored still count. `buy_err_kwh` keeps its formula. A miss in an hour with a surplus, solar or load, now reads about 7.8% larger against the plan's own sizing than before, in either direction: a solar miss there reads 7.8% larger than the plan's sizing (it read exactly), and a load miss there about 1.4% larger (it read about 6% smaller). A cloudier day or a heavier daytime house than forecast scores as a deeper under-buy, which makes the gate more likely to block. Only misses in hours without a surplus are scored as before.

**Unchanged**

- Hours without a surplus, the alarm thresholds, the grid-backstop mute of the audible runway alarm, the dispatch plan (which already counted the charge efficiency) and the MPC optimiser. There is no new option.

**Tests**

- `runwayChargeLeg.test.ts`: the step, the efficiency, the runway's change of alarm tier, the sunny-day runway, a horizon with no surplus, the planner's sizing trough, window walk, expected carry (+2.782 kWh for an hour of 5 kW sun over a 1.88 kW house, was +3.000) and force-charge start, and the ledger's `buy_err_kwh` against the planner's own re-sizing for a solar and a load miss in a surplus hour and in a deficit hour, all worked by hand. A further case shows that at `DISPATCH_ROUND_TRIP_EFFICIENCY` = 1 the planner buys 0.80 kWh below the earlier default. `runwayChargeLegPins.test.ts`: every walk calls the step, the option's descriptions name the alarm path, and the `buy_err_kwh` notes (the gate's and chapter 15-2's) name the surplus-hour load miss.

## 1.193.0

### Lifetime energy counters never step down or jump; panel counters no longer dip after a load drop

**Energy (Home Assistant)**

- Every lifetime counter the add-on publishes now only rises: PV Production, Home Consumption, Grid Import (Home), Grid to Battery Charge, Battery Energy In and Out, and each circuit. Home Assistant reads a value below 90 % of the previous one as a meter reset and books the whole new value again; it books any rise as energy. The membership re-seed and the floor/live gap repair used to step Battery Energy In and Out down to the new pool's sum, so each time the full counter went into the Energy statistics again (about 12,043 kWh on Battery Energy In by 2026-09-07; the Month and Year views read about 4.4 times high).
- The battery floors still re-seed against the new set of batteries. The published counters now continue from their last values, and the difference is kept as a basis shift: the `lifetime_basis` table, and `shiftWh` in `/api/lifetime-energy`.
- The floors, their shifts and the accepted set of Cores (the new `bms_membership` table) are written in one transaction, so a crash or a failed write can never pair a re-seeded floor with an old shift or roster. `bms-membership.json` is still written after each commit, for older releases. It is read only on the first start after the update, and rewritten when it disagrees with the database.
- A Core joining the pool counts from the re-seed. Its packs' history since their baselines is no longer published as one step up (+6,144 Wh in one read on the test plant). Energy it moves in the 15 minutes before the re-seed is not counted.
- Every counter now holds a drop between reads of up to 5 kWh at the last published value. Before, only two counters had this 5 kWh hold and the others held 50 Wh. A larger drop with no known cause continues from the last value and logs one warning naming the counter (`recorder: v1.193.0 WARN lifetime counter …`).
- A drop continued from that way stays owed (`owed_wh` in `lifetime_basis`). When the reading climbs back (a rise of over 5 kWh and at least half the amount owed), up to the amount owed is taken back off the shift and is not published as energy. Without this, a counter that read 0 and then its old value would publish twice its value: on 2026-06-08 every counter read 0 from 18:00 to 19:00, and Home Assistant booked PV Production about 808.6 kWh and Home Consumption about 825.1 kWh a second time. The owed amount survives a restart and expires 24 hours after the drop, so a drop that never comes back (a replaced database) cannot hide a later one's return. Once no more than 5 kWh is owed, every rise is taken back until nothing is. A drop that comes back in steps each under half the amount owed is published as it returns.
- Between rollups, Home Consumption, Grid Import (Home) and the circuits could read lower than a moment before after a sharp load drop: 64 to 223 Wh, and up to 3.2 kWh across a 10-minute silence at 19.2 kW. A read held the last panel reading forward to the moment of the read, and the next reading revised it. Home Assistant logged these as "not strictly increasing" and, across an hour boundary, booked a negative hour. Reads now integrate each series up to its newest reading only, so a published value lags that reading by at most one sample interval (up to 5 minutes for a steady load).
- `/api/lifetime-energy` `details` carry `shiftWh` and `heldWh`. `battery_baseline_deficit_kwh` is computed from the measured values, without the shifts. `/api/debug/battery-lifetime` reports each battery counter's shift. The lifetime carbon figures use PV Production with its shift.
- If reading the lifetime counters fails, the MQTT state and `/api/ha-state` publish their fields null (Home Assistant: unknown, not a reset) and the circuit fields follow the live circuits. The runway, the alert counts and every other field still publish.

**Documentation**

- The alerts reference gives the per-device telemetry-gap alert id as it has been since v1.188.1: `system-outage-device-<SN>-<alertStartMs ?? startMs>-3`.

**Unchanged**

- Statistics Home Assistant already recorded are not modified. Alarms, the runway and the night charge read none of these counters.

**Rollback**

- Once any counter shows a non-zero `shiftWh`, a release before this one publishes it without the shift. That is a step Home Assistant books as a meter reset (a step down of 10 % or more), as a negative hour (a smaller one) or as energy (a step up). Do not roll back past this release after a pool change.

**Not covered**

- An add-on restore of `/data` reverts the totals, the shifts and the high-water file together, so a restored counter publishes its older value.

**Tests**

- New: `lifetimeEmitGuard.test.ts` (replaces `lifetimeDipClamp.test.ts`), `recorderPoolContinuity.test.ts`, `recorderLifetimeReadMonotone.test.ts` and `helpers/haTotalIncreasing.ts` (Home Assistant's reset rule). `recorderPoolContinuity.test.ts` covers a leave and a rejoin, a restart, a failed floor commit on a leave and on a rejoin, a rebase in between, and a stale or unwritable roster file.
- `recorderFloorGapInvariant.test.ts` adds both floors above the live sum. `recorderLifetimeKeys.test.ts` adds the worker's shifted totals. `analyticsWorker.test.ts` adds the persisted keys failing. `haPayloadFmt.test.ts` adds the measured deficit and its wiring.
- Tests that asserted the step down, the pass-through of a large drop or read/rollup equality are changed, with the reason stated.
- `lifetimeEmitGuard.test.ts` adds the take-back rule and 1,000 random walks with drops that come back. `recorderEmitHighwater.test.ts` adds a counter that reads 0 and then its old value, in one process and across a restart. The new `recorderLifetimeTakeback.test.ts` covers Battery Energy In through the floors' transaction, the expiry after a replaced database, and the high-water file waiting for an uncommitted shift.
- `mutate-lifetime-monotone.mjs` is new (45 mutants). `mutate-energy-core-outage.mjs` re-points B-xviii, B-xli, B-xcvi, B-ciii and B-civ.

### README screenshots are rendered from a synthetic fleet, and nothing is written until the pixels are checked

**Documentation**

- All five README screenshots (`docs/screenshots/dashboard.png`, `solar.png`, `battery.png`, `strategy.png`, `alerts.png`) are re-rendered at 1280 px from a committed, fully synthetic fleet. The images they replace were captures of a live installation, masked by serial shape. That masking does not catch EcoFlow's default device name, "<product>-<last four digits of its serial>" until the device is renamed, or installation-specific names and figures. The paths are unchanged, so README links and the documentation build are unaffected.
- The fleet (`scripts/screenshots/fixture.mts`) has seven devices: one Smart Home Panel 2, three DELTA Pro Ultra Cores with 15 packs, an EV charger, a DELTA 3 Plus and an offline Smart Generator. Every serial is a placeholder, every device name is a product name, and the circuits keep the panel's default names. One minute-step plant model drives every card, chart and report, at a fixed clock (Wed 17 Jun 2026 12:30, America/Phoenix). Re-capturing an unchanged fixture gives byte-identical images.
- `scripts/screenshots/capture.mts` drives headless Chrome through the real built UI against `serve.mts` (127.0.0.1 only; writes are refused). It writes no image unless every tab passes all of these:
  - The page asked for no endpoint or history metric the fixture does not serve, including a read of a path the UI only writes to.
  - No card is still loading or reports itself unavailable.
  - The page's text holds no serial outside the fixture's placeholders.
  - Neither the page's text nor an OCR read of the image (full-size and downscaled) holds a device name ending in a hyphen and four digits. This covers a product name that ends in a model number, such as "Smart Home Panel 2-NNNN" or "DELTA 2-NNNN".
  - Each tab's positive controls are read, and an OCR read returns at least 20 lines.
  - The page text passes `check-no-secrets.py --stdin`.
  
  The serial rule is not applied to OCR, which can read a 0 as an O. The capture is run by hand on macOS (headless Chrome, Vision OCR). It is not run in CI.

**Checks**

- `scripts/check-no-secrets.py --stdin` applies the scan's shape rules, and the private value rules where configured, to text on standard input. A run with no flag is unchanged.
- `scripts/check-mutant-anchors.mjs` resolves `.mts` targets.

**Unchanged**

- The screenshot tooling changes no add-on code, option or behaviour.

**Tests**

  - Placeholder serials only; product names only.
  - Every API path the UI names is served, write-only or comment-only.
  - The leak gate fires on default names (a product name ending in a letter, a parenthesis or a model number) and not on dates, phone numbers or channels.
  - The replay server refuses writes, and refuses and reports a read of a write-only path.
  - One clock, and one consistent plant.
  - Each caption's element is present. The runway weekday is checked in the zone the suite runs in.
  - The capture refuses a stale bundle.
- `checkNoSecretsStdin.test.ts` runs a copy of the script in an empty directory, so a maintainer's own pattern file does not change the result.
- `mutate-screenshot-gate.mjs` is new (21 mutants).

## 1.192.0

### The mid-day charge preview states what a held reserve costs; documentation files are named Power

**Night charge (mid-day preview, nothing written)**

- The SHP2 does not discharge the pool below its backup reserve, so while a charge leg holds a raised reserve, house load the pool would have carried comes from the grid. The mid-day preview now estimates that energy for each leg it sizes, from the write at the window open to the restore, on the median load and PV the leg was planned on, and prices it: hour by hour at the tariff's rates, less what the next charge no longer buys at the mid-day rate (the energy the pool kept, over the charge efficiency). The lift to the reserve is the leg's own draw and is not counted.
- The outage backup is also sized on option B (its walk ends at the 10:00 open) beside option A (to 23:00 the next day), so the choice between them is made on real nights. Option B is a comparison only: it is never armed or announced, and the mid-day leg is still sized from option A's hold.
- On the 2026-10-14 test fixture, option A's 50% hold sends about 9.3 kWh of house load to the 12.59¢ overnight rate and adds about $0.30 a weeknight; option B's 40% hold sends about 0.6 kWh ($0.02); the mid-day leg's own hold sends nothing under the sun.
- The figures go to the evening's `night-charge[midday-shadow]:` log lines, to the preview record on the status, and to eight new ledger columns: `shadow_backup_held_import_kwh`, `shadow_backup_held_net_usd`, `shadow_cost_held_import_kwh`, `shadow_cost_held_net_usd`, `shadow_backup_b_setpoint_pct`, `shadow_backup_b_expected_buy_kwh`, `shadow_backup_b_held_import_kwh` and `shadow_backup_b_held_net_usd`. With rates not confirmed the energy is stated and nothing is priced.

**Release**

- The documentation attached to each release is named `Power-Documentation-v<version>.docx` and `.pdf`, and the files the CI documentation build produces `Power-Documentation.docx` and `.pdf` (were `EcoFlow-Panel-Documentation-…`).

**Unchanged**

- Nothing of the mid-day cycle is armed, written, pushed or spoken; the overnight charge runs as before.

**Tests**

- `heldImport.test.ts`: the held import and its price worked by hand (the lift, the discharge efficiency, a full pool's spill, the hours' rates, unpriced rates, the hold's span, the planner glue). `middayShadow.test.ts`: the evening records option A's and option B's held import on the engine's own plans, B is never probed or armed, and an older record reads back unchanged. `mutate-midday-ledger.mjs` gains ten mutants (H-i…H-x).
- The SSH console tests (`sshServer.test.ts`, `sshCaps.test.ts` and the child helper) take their host key from `generateHostKey`, as the add-on does since 1.191.7: their one shared key came from ssh2's own generator, so the 1 malformed key in 256 failed every test in the file (seen once, nine tests in one run).

## 1.191.7

### A new SSH host key is checked before it is saved

**Console**

- The SSH library (ssh2 1.17.0) drops a leading zero byte from the public half of 1 generated host key in 256, and then rejects that key as malformed. When that happened on the start that first generated the key, the SSH console stayed off for that start and the log read `console/ssh: failed to start: Malformed OpenSSH private key`; the next start replaced the key with a warning. A generated key is now read back before it is written, and one that does not parse is discarded for another (up to 8 tries). An existing host key is unaffected and keeps its fingerprint.
- The same defect failed the host-key test in about 1 CI run in 100.

## 1.191.6

### The telnet options are gone; the sign-on screen reads Plant Status System

**Before updating:** if the console was turned on with **Enable Telnet TUI** (`TELNET_ENABLED`), turn on **SSH TUI** (`SSH_ENABLED`) instead. After the update the Supervisor ignores the old option, and the console stays off until `SSH_ENABLED` is on. The port is unchanged: 2323.

- `TELNET_ENABLED`, `TELNET_PORT` and the `TELNET_HOST` fallback are removed from the options, the schema, the run script and the configuration code. **Unchanged**

## 1.191.4

### Power names itself, not EcoFlow: the Home Assistant device, notification titles and console logo; a dark fleet's forecast is no longer archived as zero

**Naming**

- The Home Assistant device is "Power" (manufacturer "Power (open-source add-on)", model "Analytics for EcoFlow SHP2 + Delta Pro Ultra"), was "EcoFlow Panel". Friendly names follow, for example "Power Alarms — Critical (P1)". Existing entity_ids are kept by Home Assistant; a fresh install mints `sensor.power_…`, and the entity reference lists those.

**Analytics**

- With every home Core dark, the 45-minute weather tick archived a next-24 h solar forecast of 0 Wh, and a short one with some Cores dark. The archive is the record a future band calibrator will score; a row is now written only when the forecast covers every connected Core (its alarm-facing and display sums agree), the solar forecast is available and no Core's first reading is pending.

## 1.191.3

### Self-consumption is cached while every Core is offline in the EcoFlow cloud; the tariff report rebuilds faster

**Analytics**

- With every home Core offline in the EcoFlow cloud after a restart, the self-consumption report was rebuilt on every read, and again inside every carbon report, which reads it: it was cached only while a Core had a reading in memory, although it is built on the panel's load and each connected Core's own recorded energy. With the tariff report, these rebuilds kept about 1 % of the reference Raspberry Pi 5's CPU core busy after 1.191.2.
- Self-consumption is now cached on the panel then too. It is rebuilt when a Core joins, leaves or returns to the panel's source list, when a Core reports again, when the house panel is re-pinned, and when the 15-minute cache expires. With no Core's reading in memory, nothing is cached while the panel lists no Core or, in the first 10 minutes after a restart, while a listed Core is online before its first reading; without the panel's reading nothing is cached, as before. The same changes now also rebuild it while Cores report, where the cached value used to stand until it expired; a source that keeps leaving and rejoining the list costs a rebuild per change, as the forecast already did.
- The tariff report integrates each hour from that hour's samples instead of searching the whole week for them: a rebuild with every Core dark takes 20 to 33 ms instead of 39 to 53 ms on the development computer.
- In a replay of the production request schedule on synthetic databases with every Core dark, the analytics worker's time falls from 143–274 to 49–80 ms a minute; with every Core reporting it stays at 9 ms.

**Unchanged**

- Every figure: on a fixed fixture, self-consumption, carbon and tariff are byte-identical to 1.191.2's, with every Core dark and with every Core reporting.
- Carbon and tariff are still cached, and their window figures published, only while a Core (a bench spare counts) has a reading in memory, as their basis flag says.
- Reports built on the forecast still read it before their own cache. That read is now a cache hit of under a microsecond, so reading their cache first would save nothing, and their figures stay tied to the forecast they were built on (1.186.5).

**Tests**

- With every Core dark, self-consumption is built once and then served with no recorder read, also inside carbon. Each change above rebuilds it, and what is served equals a fresh build on the same map. With no Core's reading in memory, a Core online before its first reading and a panel listing no Core are never cached, nor a Core without a panel (0.15.13).
- Carbon and tariff are rebuilt on every call with every Core dark, and after a restart while a Core has a reading and the panel does not yet; once the panel reports, both are cached (0.15.13). Until now no test failed when either cache was written without that basis.
- A child-process capture builds the three reports at two instants; they match 1.191.2's capture to the byte. The hourly slices equal whole-week integration on random series, at their boundaries and on unsorted input.
- `scripts/mutate-v1191-3.mjs`: 16 mutants, each killed by the case written for it; each half of the carbon and tariff cache conditions is reverted alone.

**Documentation**

- Source comments corrected, behaviour unchanged: 1.189.1, never released, reads 1.190.1; the mid-day preview runs on the evening before a winter weekday; costs are in the tariff currency, hours are the site's, the self-consumption cache lasts 15 minutes, and the add-on's only Supervisor call is a read-only list of add-ons. The option rows outside the frozen G3 golden cite their readers' current lines; the G3-pinned ones keep the captured tree's, as the golden test requires.
- The energy, architecture and solar-forecast references and the performance record describe the change. The record's oldest runtime section (2026-09-11) moves, unedited, to `docs/history/` to keep the record under its size limit, and the reference's list of history files names it.

## 1.191.2

### The day forecast is cached while every Core is offline in the EcoFlow cloud

**Analytics**

- After a restart while every Core was offline in the EcoFlow cloud, the day forecast was rebuilt for every report that reads it. No Core had a reading in memory, and the forecast was cached only with one, although it was complete: it is built on the panel's load and each connected Core's own recorded solar history. On the reference Raspberry Pi 5 each rebuild took about 1.6 s, so `/api/forecast`, `/api/runway`, `/api/forecast-skill` and `/api/confidence` each answered in about 1.6 s and `/api/ha-state` in 3 to 5 s, and the rebuilds requested by the alarm monitor, the MQTT publisher, the runway and load-shed checks and the 4-minute warm-up kept about a third of a CPU core busy without a break. In a replay of that schedule on a copy of the reference database, on a computer about three times as fast as the Pi, the alarm engine's forecast feeds took up to 1.5 s of their 2.5 s budget.
- The forecast is now cached on the panel, as it is when a Core reports. It is rebuilt when a dark Core joins or leaves the panel's source list or returns to it, when one is listed online before its first reading, when a Core reports again, and when the 30-minute cache expires. A forecast the panel's data leaves incomplete is still rebuilt after 150 s, and with neither the panel nor any Core reporting nothing is cached, as before. The same changes to the dark Cores also rebuild the forecast while other Cores report; until now the cached forecast stood until it expired.
- Each dark Core's 30-day solar history is read once per forecast build instead of twice, so a rebuild with three Cores dark takes about 40 % less time.

**Unchanged**

- Nothing the forecast shows changes: on a copy of the reference database, the forecast built with every Core dark and the one built with every Core reporting are byte-identical to 1.191.1's. The figures built on the forecast (the probabilistic band, the multi-day outlook, the dispatch plan) are still served only with the forecast they were built on; while it is cached they are now reused. With every Core reporting, the forecast is cached and rebuilt as before.

**Tests**

- With every Core dark and the panel reporting, the forecast is built once and then served with no further reads. A Core that reports again rebuilds it, and so do a dark Core that leaves or rejoins the panel's source list (also inside the 5-minute window in which the report caches' reset is deferred) and one listed online before its first reading; what is served then equals a fresh build on the same map. The three dark-Core cases fail when the cache entry does not record the dark Cores and the pending flag. A restart with every Core listed online before its first reading serves the incomplete forecast for its short window, and a fleet with no panel and no Core reporting still caches nothing.
- A capture in a child process builds the forecast on a fixed dark-fleet fixture: every recorder read of the build is distinct, and the forecast matches, to the byte, 1.191.1's capture on the same fixture.
- The 1.186.5 forecast-cache cases gain the transitions in which only the reporting Cores move (a reporting Core leaves the source list; a home with no panel gains one), which the new comparison of the dark Cores does not see.
- `scripts/mutate-v1191-2.mjs`: 9 mutants, each killed by the case written for it.

**Documentation**

- The solar-forecast reference states when the day forecast is cached and what its cache entry records. The performance record gains a section on the live measurement, its cause and the replay before and after the change.

## 1.191.1

### The console's two liveness clocks and the dashboard's Today and forecast times read the site clock

**Console**

- The 1 Hz clock in the ALARM LIST divider (ALARM screen) and in the MAIN BUS divider (BUS screen) is written in the site zone, the zone of the console's other stamps: the status header, the alarm banner and the alarm rows. Both read the host's clock, so with `SITE_TIMEZONE` set to another zone than the container's, or a container without `TZ` on the default zone, the two dividers disagreed with those stamps by the difference (two or three hours behind for a New York site on a Phoenix host, by the season; seven hours ahead for a Phoenix site on a UTC host). The SSH console and the browser console share the screens. The `HH:MM:SS` form is unchanged.

**Dashboard**

- The Today card's "since" time is written in the site zone: the card's day starts at the site's midnight, but the time was formatted in the browser's zone, so a browser elsewhere read "since 03:00 AM" or "since 07:00 AM" over the site's day. `/api/summary/today` now carries `siteTimeZone`, as `/api/night-charge/status` does.
- The Solar page's day-ahead forecast labels each hourly projection row, the projected-low tile and the runtime note with the site hour, the hour of the learned response table beside it and of the server's own forecast warning; it read the browser's clock. The Dashboard's 24-hour forecast card writes its projected-low time, axis and tooltip in the site zone too. `/api/forecast` now carries `siteTimeZone`.
- The text keeps the browser's own locale and form, so a browser in the site zone reads exactly what it did. Without a zone (a server older than the page) no time is shown rather than the browser's.

**Unchanged**

- Where the site zone is the container's zone, as it is with `SITE_TIMEZONE` unset and `TZ` set by the Supervisor, the two console clocks read exactly what they did, and a browser in that zone reads the same Today and forecast text. Nothing else changes: the computed figures, the alarms and the Home Assistant payloads are those of 1.191.0.

**Tests**

- Every clock the console prints (the two dividers, the alarm rows, the alarm banner and the status header) is read off the rendered ALARM, BUS and CONSOLE screens in child processes for a New York site on a Phoenix container, a Phoenix site on a UTC container and the reference install, against written-out times. A scan of the console's source fails on a call to any of these host-clock date helpers, with or without a locale and options: the `toLocale…String`, `toTimeString` and `toDateString` forms, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, the local `get…`/`set…` fields, `getTimezoneOffset` and a `Date` built from local fields (`new Date(y, m, …)`). The scan parses each file, so a call written across lines or nested at any depth inside another call is caught.
- The Solar page's hour labels are checked against the server's site hour in five zones and the Today card's "since" time against the site's midnight in five; the Dashboard forecast card's times are compared across three zones. Source checks also pin where each card hands the zone on or shows the time: dropping the zone from the hour rows (every row "—"), the "since" text or the projected-low time each fails.
- Fixtures in eight test files were built on the host's clock or on local hours. Each now places its instants on the site clock (or, where the code buckets by the UTC hour, on the first UTC hour that starts in the site hour, the bucket the code labels with it), so it holds and keeps its meaning under any container zone:
  - The runway's PV-basis guard asserts on the site hour `computeClipping` labels its rows with; a row labelled on the host's clock fails on a UTC container and wherever host and site differ.
  - The no-weather curtailment case places its surplus hour at a site wall time and asserts that the one estimated hour is booked at site 11:00. On a Kolkata container with a Phoenix site it read 2.5 kWh instead of 7.
  - Both held-panel curtailment cases assert that no hour of the window is curtailment. On a UTC container they passed with a missing `panel_load` read as 0 W (the 1.188.1 fix reverted).
  - The daily-figure reset cases take their instants and their expected midnights from the site's dates, not from the function under test. A one-minute boundary slop and a reading of the publish clock now fail under every zone pairing; a day start on the host's clock fails wherever host and site differ.
  - The display-versus-alarm PV contract now exercises its bias-factor cause as well as the coverage gate: a display sum that drops the bias factor fails.
  - The per-Core shade report places its clear hours in the first UTC hour that starts in each site hour, as the report labels them, and holds on a site whose daylight saving ends inside the fixture (Auckland, and Lord Howe Island, whose clock moves by half an hour), where real uniform shade was no longer detected. The two-Core gap case passed the summed-fleet calculation the per-Core report replaced; it now also puts the gap on the six most recent days, and a case with one Core of three dark on those days is added: both fail the summed fleet (a phantom 50 % and 33 % shortfall on every clear hour). A case with shade on most recent days fails a median reference in place of the 90th percentile.
  - The realized-irradiance training case and the soiling charge-taper cases key their rows on the UTC hour, as the recorder and the weather feed do, and hold on half- and quarter-hour zones (Kolkata, Kathmandu, Adelaide, St John's).
- The forecast-skill cache case scores the realized and the first-write reports against one forecast. A cached report is served only for the forecast it was scored against, so a fresh forecast for each call missed the cache whatever its key, and a cache keyed by the window alone (a realized report served to the band calibrator) passed the case; it now fails.
- Test comments that said the code reads the host's clock now name the site clock (clipping, forecast, rate table, dispatch, solar-model metrics, the settings-drift quiet window, the message-rate floor, the diurnal backtest baseline, the golden capture), and the forecast's band-check failure messages print the site hour.

**Documentation**

- The user-interface reference describes the console's clocks, the Today card's "since" time and the forecast cards' hour labels; the solar-forecast reference names the field `/api/forecast` adds.

## 1.191.0

### The site clock, the tariff, the PV array, the devices and the plant limits are options; unset keeps today's behaviour

**Configuration**

- `server/src/config.ts` now carries the table of every add-on option, every environment knob the add-on reads and the deployment constants, each with the parse rule its reader applies today (the four truthiness conventions, the blank and `null` rules, the clamps). Nothing changes for a stored configuration: a parity test compares each option's value when the variable is absent, blank or cleared with the shipped default, and every difference is declared with its reason. New keys from here on are optional, have no default and are exported only when set, so an unset key leaves the behaviour as it is.
- Eight golden captures pin what the code computes on the reference install's settings: the site clock, the tariff, every option's parse, the night-charge schedule, the PV physics, the panel and spare topology, the MQTT discovery payloads and the plant limits. They are frozen by checksum; a change needs a visible manifest change in the same diff. With every new option unset, all eight match what 1.190.2 computes.
- 38 new options, all optional with no default, listed under **Show unused optional configuration options**. While a key is unset it is not passed to the server, and the code takes the path it took before.
- A new install ships with `BROADCAST_BILINGUAL` off: the Spanish second pass plays once it is turned on and a Spanish voice is named. An install that has saved its configuration keeps the value it stored. The other defaults that came from the reference plant stay as they are: `FORECAST_LAT` / `FORECAST_LON` remain the placeholder the 50 km notices are measured from, `BROADCAST_AUDIO_BASE` is Home Assistant's own host name and this add-on's port, and `ARB_GRID_INPUT_CAP_KW` keeps 17 because no value is neutral: 0 turns the contention model off and times the force-charge at a fixed rate about twice what one Core takes, so a one-Core plant would start late. The setup checklist asks every home to enter its grid-input breaker capacity.
- `GET /api/site` serves the site time zone and its source, the coordinates and their source, the currency, the PV string layout and each Core's own strings, the PV array the physics uses, the solar assumptions the web draws with and the mains voltages; per Core, whether it is a bench spare, only while `BENCH_SPARE_SNS` is set.

**Site clock**

- `SITE_TIMEZONE` names the IANA time zone every local date, hour and clock time is computed in: the tariff periods, the night-charge window and its evening notice, quiet hours, the morning digest, the daily totals, the statistics import and the console's stamps. Unset, the zone is the container's `TZ`, which the Supervisor sets to Home Assistant's zone, and `America/Phoenix` when neither is set. The zone is resolved once at start and never switched while the add-on runs; the start-up log names it and its source.
- A configured zone the runtime cannot resolve raises a repair issue and the next source applies; it never becomes UTC silently. A zone that differs from Home Assistant's raises a warning and a repair issue. Links of the legacy zone, such as `US/Arizona`, read as `America/Phoenix`.
- The fixed UTC−7 arithmetic and the reads of the host's own clock are replaced by the site zone: day starts, the statistics noon, day loops that cross a daylight-saving change, and the hour index of the MPC tariff vector.
- The on-peak hours the cost figures, the dispatch planner and the MPC vector fall back to while rates are unconfirmed are judged on the site's hour and weekday, and the times in the telemetry-gap and outage alerts are written in the site zone. Both read the host's clock: with `SITE_TIMEZONE` set to another zone than the host's, a New York plan on a Phoenix host was priced on-peak three hours late and an outage at 14:00 read 11:00 AM. Identical where the site zone is the host's.
- The web writes the night-charge window, the cancel deadline and the mid-day shadow in the site zone the server reports, and "today" on the circuit card and the Solar page starts at the site's midnight. A browser in another zone showed shifted hours and asked the server for a different day.
- In `America/Phoenix` the site clock equals the fixed-offset arithmetic at every instant (goldens G1 and G4, every hour of 2025–2027).

**Tariff**

- The tariff is no longer APS-only. `TARIFF_PLAN` picks `aps_r_ev` (the built-in R-EV table, which stays the default while the option is unset), `flat` (`TARIFF_FLAT_CENTS_PER_KWH` every hour), `two_tier` (one on-peak window, `TARIFF_ON_PEAK_HOURS` on `TARIFF_ON_PEAK_DAYS`, at `TARIFF_ON_PEAK_CENTS` and `TARIFF_OFF_PEAK_CENTS`) or `custom`, a period table written in `TARIFF_PERIODS` and `TARIFF_RATES` (for example `on_peak 16-19 mon-fri all onpeak; overnight 23-05 mon-fri all cheap` with `on_peak=31.2/22.5; off_peak=16.9/15.1; overnight=12.6`). The R-EV table written in that grammar parses to the built-in model exactly, labels apart; a custom plan's labels come from its hours.
- For every plan: `TARIFF_SUMMER_MONTHS` (`4-9` when unset; a range may wrap the year, `10-3`), `TARIFF_HOLIDAYS` (`aps`, `none` or a list of dates), `TARIFF_FIXED_DAILY_CENTS`, `TARIFF_RATES_CONFIRMED` (unset takes `TARIFF_APS_RATES_CONFIRMED`) and `NIGHT_CHARGE_CHEAP_PERIOD`, the period the night charge plans in (a custom plan's period flagged `cheap`; `overnight` on the R-EV table). The `TARIFF_APS_*` options keep their names and remain the R-EV table's rates.
- The tariff settings the code read only from the environment until now are options: `TARIFF_FLAT_CENTS_PER_KWH`, `TARIFF_ON_PEAK_CENTS`, `TARIFF_OFF_PEAK_CENTS`, `TARIFF_EXPORT_CENTS_PER_KWH`, `TARIFF_ON_PEAK_HOURS` and `TARIFF_ON_PEAK_DAYS`, each read as before while unset. One reader serves the cost figures, the dispatch optimiser and the MPC vector; the flat 17 ¢ fallback is one constant instead of three copies.
- With `TARIFF_PLAN` set, the MPC vector prices an hour no confirmed rate covers with the cost figures' own pair: an unconfirmed `two_tier` plan's two rates. It read the environment-only `…_CENTS_PER_KWH` pair, which no option sets, so it priced every hour at the 17 ¢ flat default while the cost figures used the plan's rates. While `TARIFF_PLAN` is unset the MPC keeps its own pair (golden G2).
- A tariff setting that cannot be read fails closed: every price reads unknown, the cost figures use the flat fallback, no night-charge window is planned, and a repair issue names the option. It never falls back to the R-EV table.
- `TARIFF_CURRENCY` (USD when unset; EUR, GBP, CAD or AUD) sets the unit of the Home Assistant cost and rate sensors and the symbol in the alert and dispatch text; `/api/site` reports it. An unknown code keeps USD and raises a repair issue.
- With every new option unset nothing changes on an existing install: the tariff model, the cost figures, the discovery payloads and the text are byte-identical (goldens G2 and G7). Declared: the R-EV holidays after 2045 are computed instead of missing; the cost figures keep their above-zero rule for a rate (a 0 ¢ period is priced at 0 by the rate table only); while `TARIFF_PLAN` is unset the cost figures and the MPC vector keep reading their own two-tier option names, which only the `two_tier` plan treats as aliases.
- The two round-trip efficiencies, 0.86 for the night-charge sizing and 0.9 for the MPC, are named side by side; the values are unchanged.

**Night charge**

- The planner plans in the tariff's own cheap period at every step: tonight's window, the end of its horizon, the cycle chooser, the long-gap rule and the on-peak hours a scored night is credited with. Each named the R-EV period `overnight`, so a custom plan whose cheap period has another name got no window ("hold (no charge window)" every night), a plan with a dearer period called `overnight` was planned in that one, and `NIGHT_CHARGE_CHEAP_PERIOD` changed nothing. A `two_tier` plan still has no cheap window unless `NIGHT_CHARGE_CHEAP_PERIOD` is `off_peak`, which makes the off-peak hours the window.
- With any plan other than the R-EV preset, a charge window is one night of the cheap period: a run of it inside the plan's nightly window, ending where the next night's opens. With `off_peak` as the cheap period and an on-peak period on weekdays only, the weekend is one off-peak run (Friday 19:00 to Monday 14:00 with on-peak 14-19). Friday's window ended Saturday evening, and Saturday's and Sunday's plans resolved a window that had opened a day or more earlier, which a write mode refuses, so nothing charged before Monday's on-peak. Each evening now plans its own night (Friday 19:00 to Saturday 14:00, then Saturday's, then Sunday 19:00 to Monday 14:00), and the next window opens the next evening. The R-EV preset's windows are unchanged (golden G4).
- With a plan other than the R-EV preset, the nightly job's schedule follows the plan's cheap window: the job runs until the window opens (at most midnight), its hour is clamped to the hour before the open (at most 22) with a start-up warning and a repair issue, a stale panel reading defers the plan until the earlier of an hour after the notify time and 30 minutes before the open, a row with no stored window is scored on the plan's own night, a window shorter than 3 hours still counts as a full night, and a force-charge may run for the window's length plus an hour (never less than 7 hours). A cheap window that opened at or before 21:00 was planned at 21:30 inside it, and a write mode refused every night.
- With the R-EV preset the schedule keeps its values whatever the notify time: until 23:00, the hour at most 22, the deferral until 22:30, 3 hours and 7 hours (golden G4).

**PV array and site location**

- `PV_ARRAY_KWP`, `PV_TILT_DEG` and `PV_AZIMUTH_DEG` describe the array the clear-sky physics model uses. Once any `PV_*` key is set the model uses that array at `FORECAST_LAT` / `FORECAST_LON`, the weather's hourly temperature in place of a fixed 30 °C, and, for the curtailment estimate, the site's own clear-sky noon irradiance, never above the 900 W/m² used before. While no `PV_*` key is set the model is the reference array, unchanged (golden G5).
- `PV_STRINGS` gives each Core's high- and low-voltage strings, with an override per panel slot or Core name (`hv=10x400,lv=4x400; slot2=hv=8x450`), and the Solar page draws them. A value that does not parse keeps the default layout and raises a repair issue; a total that disagrees with `PV_ARRAY_KWP` is a start-up warning.
- `SITE_LOCATION_FROM_HA` takes the coordinates from Home Assistant's home location. It is read in the background after a start, saved, and applied from the next start, so the coordinates never change while the add-on runs. Off, a start-up notice and a repair issue appear when Home Assistant's home is more than 50 km from `FORECAST_LAT` / `FORECAST_LON`.
- One notice and repair issue, "the reference home's defaults are in effect", appears when the site zone is not `America/Phoenix` while `TARIFF_PLAN` is unset, or when the site is more than 50 km from the placeholder coordinates while no `PV_*` key is set.
- The web's solar assumptions follow the site: the forecast's orientation text takes the hemisphere from the latitude, and the daylight band and solar noon come from the coordinates and the zone. On the reference array both keep the bands they had.

**Devices**

- `BENCH_SPARE_SNS` lists the bench-spare Cores by serial, or `none`. When set it replaces the built-in spare list, never adds to it, everywhere that list is read: the offline-alarm mute and the three home-pool fallbacks used while no panel roster is known. The roster override still applies on top. A serial that matches no device raises a repair issue. Unset, the built-in list applies as before, and the built-in list itself is unchanged.
- `DEVICE_ALIASES` (JSON, serial to display name) is merged over `/data/device-aliases.json`, which is merged over the image's own file. A layer that cannot be read is skipped and raises a repair issue.
- A Core with no name of its own is numbered by its panel slot, and two such Cores get distinct names (the slot, else the serial's last four characters). The repair cards and the insight rows no longer print "Core null".
- The warranty export's default chassis is chosen from the devices present, and the defective-pack alerts link the export with their own chassis's serial.
- The session self-heal quorum is the smaller of `SELF_HEAL_MIN_DEVICES` and the number of devices on the account, so an account with fewer devices than the quorum can still trigger it.

**Plant limits**

- EV: `EV_MAX_LOAD_W`, `EV_CHARGER_COUNT` (0: no charger; 1: overlapping predicted sessions are alternatives, as before; 2–4: they add up, capped at the count × `EV_MAX_LOAD_W`), `EV_PLATEAU_MIN_W` and `EV_CIRCUITS`, the circuits the EV detection scans. `EV_MAX_LOAD_W` now has one reader; the night-charge planner parsed it a second time, unclamped.
- `FORCE_CHARGE_KW_PER_CORE` (5.5 kW when unset) times the just-in-time force-charge start and sizes the planner's automatic charge cap; `ARB_CHARGE_CAP_KW` above 0 still sets the cap.
- `RUNWAY_POOL_OVERHEAD_FLOOR_W`, `RUNWAY_CORE_OVERHEAD_W`, `BMS_RESEED_MIN_GAP_WH`, `CAPACITY_SCALE_MIN`, `FORECAST_NIGHT_START_HOUR`, `FORECAST_NIGHT_END_HOUR`, `GRID_CO2_INTENSITY_LB_PER_MWH` and `CYCLING_BASE_WEAR_USD_PER_KWH`, read until now from the environment only, are options; each schema range equals the clamp the code applies.
- `OPPORTUNISTIC_LOADS` (`id:watts:category[:label]` entries, or `none`) replaces the built-in list of loads the surplus advisor suggests, and `BATTERY_SOC_LADDER` (`pct:tier` entries) the levels the SoC alarm speaks at. Unset, the built-in list and the 50/40/30/20/15/10/8/4/2 ladder apply (golden G8).

**Wording that described one home**

- The forecast-dip rationale compares with "typical clear sky", not one city's.
- The host under-voltage alert names the host that runs the monitor, not a Raspberry Pi; `HOST_POWER_ENTITY` can name any under-voltage `binary_sensor`.
- The forecast-ensemble note on the Advanced Insights card says "monsoon-season clouds".
- The night-charge card is titled "Night-charge plan": the plan is for the tariff's next cheap window, which is not overnight on every tariff.
- The spoken priority previews name Core 1, which every plant has, in place of Cores 2 and 3.
- The console's station label reads GRID-TIED PLANT while the grid resolver sees a grid and OFF-GRID PLANT while islanded; it read OFF-GRID PLANT on every plant.

**Documentation**

- A setup checklist, `docs/guide/your-home.md`, lists what differs from the reference deployment and what to measure for each: the time zone (normally Home Assistant's), the forecast coordinates (a placeholder by default), the tariff plan with its periods, rates, seasons, holidays, fixed charge and currency, the PV array and its strings per panel slot, EV charging, bench spares, device names, the grid-input breaker capacity, the per-Core force-charge rate, the runway overhead for fewer than three Cores, and the carbon and wear factors. It also says to set the panel's own time zone in the EcoFlow app to match Home Assistant, which Power cannot check, and that a time zone whose UTC offset is not a whole hour is not supported. The operator guide links it from Getting started, and the printable manual includes it.
- The operator guide's scope names `TARIFF_PLAN` (APS R-EV built in and the default) and the site time zone, `SITE_TIMEZONE` (empty means Home Assistant's zone), and states the remaining limits: English and Spanish only, and a second panel with only its own charge levels and runway. The night-charge notice is described for the tariff's cheap window in site time.
- The option reference has a row for every new optional key, each stating what Power does while it is unset; the APS rate fields are labelled as the APS R-EV preset on the Configuration page and in the reference.
- The Configuration-page help no longer quotes one plant's measured kW per Core, cites a past incident or gives one installation's handset as the SIP example; the envelope option asks for the grid-input breaker capacity, and the retention help states the 7–3650-day range the schema enforces.
- In the engineering reference, figures measured on the reference deployment are labelled "reference plant", knobs are marked add-on or environment-only, and passages that called the clock, the tariff, the PV site or the opportunistic loads fixed name the options that now set them. The reference deployment's own Core roster and circuit-1 note move to `docs/history/reference-plant-notes.md`. The night-charge design record and the performance record are labelled as the reference plant's.
- `server/.env.example` lists every add-on option, generated from `config.yaml` and the option table; it no longer carries the notification channels removed earlier.

## 1.190.2

### The Today card counts the energy measured at the panel while the Cores are dark

**Dashboard**

- While a home Core reports nothing of its own, the Today card's Solar produced, AC output and Batteries (net) now count the energy the panel's meter on that Core's battery slot measured for it — the figures Home Assistant's Energy counters already add — in place of the Core's own readings, which are not recorded while it is dark. On 19 October, with every Core offline since 14 October and the house on the batteries, the card read 0 Wh for all three and "25% measured" while those counters read 41.3 kWh of solar, 34.5 kWh into the batteries and 9.4 kWh out of them since midnight. For each stretch a Core is measured at the panel after the update, the card reads what the counters counted for it over the same stretch.
- A figure with a part measured at the panel says "via panel" under it. Solar the panel could only work out from the Core's output and the rise in its charge level — before the panel's own solar reading has passed its check — is a lower bound and says "via panel · lower bound" ("partly a lower bound" when only some of the day's is). No solar is counted for a dark Core at night, so an outage that is over by sunrise leaves Solar produced unmarked. Batteries (net) reads, for example, "charged · via panel".
- "% measured" counts the time the panel's meter covered each dark Core, so an all-dark day measured at the panel reads close to 100 % instead of 25 %.
- A Core that reports for part of the day counts its own readings for that part and the panel's for the rest, handing over at the same instants as the energy counters, so no stretch is counted twice — also when a Core's own readings come back while the panel is still measuring it (its data arriving before the cloud lists it online again).
- The Solar tab's Today tile shows the same solar figure with the same note.
- A day with every Core reporting reads exactly as before.
- From the update onward: the panel-measured energy of a dark Core is recorded for the card at each 5-minute count, so on the day of the update the card counts it only from the update on, and its figures and "% measured" stay below the counters' for that day. The record is kept as long as the recorded readings.

**Documentation**

- The energy reference describes the record the card reads and how it meets the Cores' own readings; the user-interface reference describes the card's notes.

## 1.190.1

### The panel card names the per-battery charge limit; the Cleared list opens on 7 days; the live solar reading stays trusted; the Midday-Charge window sensors are timestamps again

**Dashboard**

- The Smart Home Panel card's "Charge power 7.20 kW" is now "Charge limit (per battery) 7.20 kW × 3 connected = 21.60 kW".
